leads.name: sierkers amsterdam
leads.reason: Single-sourced. Japanese ornamental cherry 'Kanzan' (Prunus serrulata 'Kanzan') in the garden behind Huize Frankendael, Middenweg 116, planted circa 1920 per bomenbieb. Tried monumentaltrees.com's park Frankendael listing (6 registered monumental trees there) as a second source but the page 403s every fetch and search snippets alone are not enough to confirm this specific tree is among them (per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's rule that a search summary is a lead, not a source). The Rijksmonument description of the Frankendael garden layout (rijksmonumenten.nl/monument/422421) names beeches, chestnuts, oaks and limes but does not mention a cherry. Vrienden van Frankendael's own site and Amsterdam's official bijzondere-bomen map are both JS-rendered/403 and could not be checked. A future pass with browser access to monumentaltrees.com or a direct look at Amsterdam's bomen.amsterdam.nl register for Middenweg 116 could likely resolve this quickly.

blocked.name: duiveltjesiep utrecht
blocked.reason: Dead. bomenbieb records alive_per_source Ja but this is stale: RTV Utrecht (2026) and UStad report the original 184-year-old duiveltjesiep behind the Centraal Museum died of Dutch elm disease in 2022; the trunk was left standing for insects/birds/fungi and three cuttings were replanted (two in Amelisweerd, one near the stump), none of which is the same collectible specimen. Never ships as this entry. The replanted cuttings are too young (2022 or later) to qualify on their own merit; not pursued further this pass.
